claim: Method and limits: 71 reviews read individually in the original language, hand-coded (78 codes in 12 families, all used; 19 unions), 30 pre-write checks incl. 14 semantic re-derivations from text, verify-after-write; no duplicates, no repeat authors, no edits; one review = 1.41% so the spec's bands cannot discriminate (4 reviews already 'High-priority') — every headline carries a Wilson 95% CI, and 'where a band and an interval disagree, trust the interval'; no storefront reaches 50 (de 17, in 10, us 10) — no standalone country claims; 14 of 71 (19.72%) are content-free 5★ ('Love it') — excluding them: mean 4.31 → 4.14★, money-negative 19.72% → 24.56%, concept-positive 26.76% → 33.33% (verbatim) Measure | Full corpus (n=71) | Excluding low-info (n=57) ; Mean rating | 4.31★ | 4.14★ ; Money-negative | 19.72% | 24.56% ; Any praise | 84.51% | 82.46% ; Concept-positive | 26.76% | 33.33%; only 4 reviewers state they paid (+1 implied) — no conversion, renewal, refund or churn rate; Apple publishes no release before v2.6.4 (2025-09-29) so 36 of 71 cannot be tied to a release; 10 SKUs carry no periods so the report cannot say which are subscriptions; 2 of 21 months have zero reviews.

Selection bias quantified: 71 text reviews sit on a public base of 339 ratings across the same 28 storefronts — ratings-weighted public mean 4.58★ vs corpus 4.31★ (gap −0.27); 268 people rated without writing; every complaint share is a share of people who chose to write.

claim: §8.4.1 lead with the concept everywhere because it is the only thing with no detractors — the description and ASO title already do; the paywall does not: 'a user who converts is converting on the concept, and the concept is experienceable only with more than one habit'.

§8.4.2 reconsider the one-habit cap on strategy grounds, not review grounds — the report does not recommend raising it (no conversion data), but the decision should be made knowing that at one habit the product's own differentiator (forgiving multi-habit momentum) is not experienceable free, and that the reviewers who did convert converted on comparative value against trackers they had already tried — an informed judgement they could only make after using it. §8.5 do not: fund a reliability push ahead of disclosure (0 defects in 37 reviews / 12 months; the one open question is Apple Health); treat the 5★ share as satisfaction (17 of 50 five-star reviews, 34%, do not evidence satisfaction with anything); read the 2026 rating recovery as the monetization problem resolving (volume flat, complaints moved into 4–5★); build from the request backlog as a list (14 of 16 single-voice, one reviewer accounts for five); draw a country conclusion.

§8.7 research questions: does a lifetime SKU currently exist (answerable in one minute in App Store Connect); what is the free-tier limit today and has it changed; what do the 268 silent raters think (0.27★ higher); why did the 1★ reviews stop on 2025-11-03; did Badges and the Habit Forest work (one mention between them); what happens after purchase (two of four payers had a bad experience, zero refund/cancellation mentions — the largest blank); why are Japan, Australia and Taiwan silent despite a shipped Japanese localisation.

A forgiving score that decays instead of resetting is the whole value — 'missing a day does not reset / no guilt, punishment, anxiety or pressure' (CONCEPT_FORGIVING 11, 4.82★); 'I used to drop habits the second I missed a day — all because of streak pressure'; the streak is still shown alongside for those who want it.
